name: settlement-commands
description: Tier 1 command gate. Keep the install step named "install" — the harness fingerprints it to skip reinstalling across attempts. EVERY command invokes the VENDORED yarn explicitly. The harness hands these straight to a shell rather than resolving the package manager the way it does for baseline.commands, so a bare `yarn` dies with "command not found" on any machine without a global install — which is every machine relying on this repo's vendored Yarn 3, since `corepack enable` needs Administrator on Windows. The symptom is all five commands failing in ~50ms, which reads like a broken project rather than a missing binary.

commands.name: install
commands.purpose: Install workspace dependencies. Plain install, no --no-immutable: the committed lockfile is in sync, so this matches what CI does.

commands.name: lint
commands.purpose: ESLint across both workspaces. Must report zero errors.

commands.name: test
commands.purpose: 132 unit tests over the framework-free core: the evidence builder's refusals, the feed table, the HCS reader against fabricated mirror-node responses, the scheduling guards, and a check that every invariant points at a test file that exists. Hermetic and offline — the live-endpoint suite is deliberately separate so this never fails because testnet was slow.

commands.name: contract-test
commands.purpose: 65 contract tests, one file per invariant plus a parity check between the deploy script's feed table and the one the UI reads. Uses test:ci, which skips the gas reporter. Neither script enables HEDERA_FORKING: the scaffold ships networks.hardhat.forking unconditional, which sends every deploy and call to Hashio and takes the suite from 12 seconds to 10 minutes while fetching nothing it needs — the feed under test is a local mock, deployed so a bound can be exercised at an age no live feed would ever show.

commands.name: build
commands.purpose: Production build, which also type-checks. The type check is load-bearing here: it is what caught setPayerAccountId being handed a string where an AccountId belongs, on a path that costs HBAR to reach.
